items.question: Who is CourtFlux for?
items.answer: CourtFlux is being built for basketball players, coaches, teams, academies and performance analysts who want to get more useful information from the game film they already record.

items.question: What can CourtFlux understand today?
items.answer: The current system tracks players, teams and the ball and includes a P2 basketball-state layer for ball control, possession changes, loose-ball sequences, shot attempts and candidate pass, turnover and rebound events. Formal event and attribution accuracy is still being validated against reviewed human ground truth.

items.question: Do I need specialist cameras?
items.answer: No proprietary capture system is required. CourtFlux is designed around ordinary basketball game film, although camera position, resolution, occlusion and motion blur can affect analysis quality.

items.question: How will the free trial work?
items.answer: The launch model is a 14-day trial with no credit card required and one game of up to 60 minutes included. During the private beta, billing and trial enforcement are not yet active.

items.question: Does CourtFlux replace the coach or analyst?
items.answer: No. CourtFlux is intended to structure evidence, reduce manual video work and help people review the game faster while keeping basketball judgement with the player, coach or analyst.

items.question: How do game allowances work?
items.answer: Plans are presented in approximate full games because that is how coaches think about usage. Under the hood, usage is measured by processed video duration: Coach includes 300 analysis minutes and Team includes 1,000 per month.
